wu: Two Truths and a Lie: Students write three sentences about their free time (e.g., 'I play football', 'I watch TV', 'I speak Spanish'), then share with a partner who guesses the lie. Teacher models first with own sentences.
wuAlt: Find Someone Who: Students walk around asking 'Do you...?' questions (e.g., 'Do you play video games?') and tally responses on a bingo sheet.
Free Time Charades: Students act out free time activities (e.g., 'swimming', 'reading') while classmates guess the verb phrase.
pres: Show flashcards of free time activities (e.g., football, cinema, music). Model KET Part 1 frames: 'What do you like doing in your free time?' and 'I like...' with answers. Elicit responses from students and check understanding with thumbs up/down for correct/incorrect answers.
presAlt: Realia Display: Bring in props (e.g., football, book, headphones) and ask 'What do you do with this?' to elicit activity vocabulary.
Dialogue Modeling: Teacher and student role-play a short conversation using KET frames, then students repeat in pairs.
prac: KET Part 1 Drill: Students practice asking and answering 'What do you like doing?' with a partner using flashcards. Teacher circulates to correct pronunciation and provide sentence starters like 'I like...' or 'I don't like...'.
pracAlt: Matching Game: Students match activity pictures to verb phrases (e.g., 'play football') and then use them in sentences.
Chain Reaction: One student says 'I like...', the next repeats it and adds their own, building a chain.
ls: KET Listening Part 2: Play a recording of two friends discussing free time activities. Students listen and tick the activities they hear (e.g., 'swimming', 'cinema') on a worksheet. Check answers as a class.
re: Free Time Relay: Divide class into two teams. One student runs to the board, writes an activity verb (e.g., 'play'), and returns to tag the next, who adds the noun (e.g., 'football'). Fastest team wins.
prod: Mock KET Speaking Part 2: Students work in pairs. Student A describes their free time preferences using 'I like...' and 'I don't like...'. Student B asks follow-up questions like 'Why?' or 'When do you...?'. Teacher uses a rubric to observe and note strengths/areas for improvement.
rw: KET Reading Part 3 Practice: Students read a short text about a teenager's free time (e.g., 'My name is Sam. I like football and music.') and answer multiple-choice questions (e.g., 'What does Sam like?') by circling A, B, or C.
st: Sing 'What Do You Like to Do?' song with actions (e.g., 'clap hands' for 'clap hands'). Close with: 'Today we practiced KET speaking questions about free time. Thank you, class!'
g: One student mimes an activity (e.g., 'swimming') while others guess using 'Do you...?'
Students listen to teacher call out activities and mark them on their bingo cards
Students match activity pictures to verb phrases on cards
Students ask 'What do you like doing?' to three classmates in 2 minutes each
diff: Fast finishers: Write 3 sentences about a friend's free time using 'He/She likes...'.
Support: Use sentence frames ('I like...') and picture prompts during the mock speaking task.
hw: Record yourself answering 'What do you like doing in your free time?' and send to teacher.
Write 5 questions to ask a friend about their free time.
Draw 3 free time activities and label them in English.
tip: Encourage students to use 'I like...' and 'I don't like...' naturally, not just memorized answers. Pair stronger students with weaker ones to build confidence during mock exams.
